$comment: Licence policy, version 2. Rewritten 2026-11-18 for the approach of 2026-11-18 (PG-D27).

The one machine-readable licence whitelist of this repository (PG-D3; T1 R7). Three scripts read it: .github/scripts/check-licences.mjs judges every dependency and record against it, .github/scripts/generate-notices.mjs writes THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md from its platform entries, its nuget clarifications and its licence_texts, crate_texts and source_links, and .github/scripts/licence-configs.mjs generates deny.toml, about.toml, .github/dependency-review-config.yml and the three nuget-license files .github/nuget-license/allowed-licenses.json, overrides.json (from the nuget clarifications) and licensefile-mappings.json (always {}, because a nuget clarification pins the installed file, never a committed copy; nuget-license is still given the file) from it (T1 R8). Change this file, then run `node .github/scripts/licence-configs.mjs --write`; CI runs `--check` and fails on any drift. The lists follow knowledge/licensing.md (§2.3 the whitelist, §2.6 patents, §8.5 the gate) and engineering-standard.md §3.10.

Nobody accepts a licence by hand (PG-D2; AP §1). A licence that is not on the allow list of its class and profile fails. The agent then writes a clarification (the true licence is on the list, with evidence and the licence file's SHA-256), replaces the dependency, or drops the part. There is no exception list and no expiry date. Luka is never asked about a licence.

profile (PG-D1; T1 R2): gpl = GPL-3.0-or-later without the linking exception; gpl-le = with the GPL linking exception (PerfWindow PW-D12, Instructium IN-D13); reserved = the CV; permissive = a repository not yet relicensed. Set it when the template is adopted; both scripts refuse to run while it is the placeholder.

classes (PG-D1; T1 R1): L linked code, F fonts, C content and data, M model weights, P platform components, T build and CI tools (never shipped). Package-manager trees are class L unless class_overrides names a package; vendored files take the class of their REUSE.toml path group. Classes F, C, M and T are the same in every profile; only L depends on the profile.

deny: SPDX id (a * glob is allowed) -> the reason the gate prints. It applies to classes L, F, C and M and to toolchain runtimes, and wins over every allow list, except that tier2 licences pass on a pointer record of class C or M (PG-D2). Ids not in deny and not on an allow list fail too, with the generic reason. Class T and the separate programs and upstream binaries of class P use only their own allow lists, because combining is not at stake there (T1 R4, §2.6; PG-D36 (3)).
allow.P: per platform kind. A toolchain runtime is linked into our binaries, so its licence must also pass the profile's class-L list, or be one of the ids listed for it here.

tier2 (PG-D2, PG-D33 (4)): data and model licences that are fetched only by the user's explicit action from where they are published, with the licence shown first; never committed, bundled, hosted, preselected, recommended or the default. A model's tier is the most restrictive of its own licence and its datasets' licences; a dataset with no stated licence, or with a US-only status, makes it tier 2 at most.

pointer_only (PG-D33): a record of such a class must be a pointer (kind: pointer), fetched from the rights holder's own upload at the user's action. No model file is bundled, hosted, committed, published, uploaded as a CI artifact or attached to a release.

licence_refs: LicenseRef- ids this policy defines. requires: fields a record that carries the id must have. LicenseRef-PD-USGov and LicenseRef-Public-Domain-US-Government need a second_basis (PG-D32): { basis: A|B|C, evidence, url, read, sha256 }. An id with requires is never written into a tool config, because only the record check can see the fields.

class_overrides: { ecosystem: cargo|npm|nuget|pypi|maven, package, class, why }. A package judged under another class, such as a crate or npm package that bundles fonts (class F; T1 R9). In deny.toml it becomes a [[licenses.exceptions]] entry for that crate only.
lgpl_dynamic (gpl-le only; T1 R2): { ecosystem, package, file, sha256, why }. An LGPL library allowed only as a separately loaded, replaceable file.

clarifications (T1 R6): { ecosystem, package, version, licence, evidence, read (YYYY-MM-DD), licence_file: { path, sha256, cargo_deny_hash (cargo only) } }. The licence must pass its class and profile. path is relative to the crate root for cargo. For nuget it names the installed file, ~/.nuget/packages/<id in lower case>/<version in lower case>/<file>: nuget-license reports no install path, so {path} cannot be found, and the generated overrides.json gives the package its licence by id and version alone, whatever the package's own file holds, so a committed copy as the pin would not pin the package (B0-U13, 2026-11-25: with the installed file as the pin, a changed installed file and a repack with the same id and version each failed with 'its clarification no longer holds'; with a committed copy as the pin, a changed installed file passed). licence-configs.mjs, and check-licences.mjs, which reads the policy through it, therefore refuse a nuget clarification whose path is a copy in the repository as a malformed policy (exit 2; B0-U01). For the other ecosystems path may use {path} (the install path the tool reports), ~/ or a path from the repository root. A changed licence file fails the gate, and a clarification that matches no package of its ecosystem is spent and fails.

licence_texts (B0-U04, B0-U13): { licence, source, read (YYYY-MM-DD), licence_file, sha256 }. The pinned text of a licence that a NuGet package declares as an SPDX expression but does not ship. One entry per licence: a WITH expression such as "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception" is one licence, and an expression with AND or OR needs a text for each licence in it. The text is committed under .github/licence-texts/ exactly as its source publishes it; licence_file is its path from the repository root (or ~/), and sha256 null means not pinned yet, which fails when a package needs the text. generate-notices.mjs checks licence, licence_file and sha256, names a licence pinned twice as a problem, and writes each text once with the Copyright line of every package that uses it.

crate_texts (B0-U04, B0-U12): { package, version, source, read, why, files: [{ path, sha256 }] }, or { crates: ["name version", ...], source, read, why, files } in place of package and version for crates of one repository that share their texts (the egui crates). The licence text of a crate whose package ships no LICENSE, LICENCE or COPYING file, for which cargo-about writes only the SPDX template, which names no copyright holder. Each path is from the repository root (or ~/), and sha256 null means not pinned yet, which fails when the report holds the crate. generate-notices.mjs reads the list with --cargo-about only: a malformed entry and a crate listed twice are named problems, and an entry for a crate that the report does not hold is a note on stderr that does not fail the run (a per-installer report holds fewer crates). A committed text is the bytes of the upstream's git blob, never a Windows working-tree copy (core.autocrlf may have changed its line ends), taken at the commit that the crate's package records in .cargo_vcs_info.json, or at the release tag where that commit is not served (egui 0.37.0; B0-U12).

source_links: { ecosystem (cargo or nuget), package, version, url (https) }. The page that the Source column of THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md names for a package where the project's own URL is not where its licence points (an MPL-2.0 component gets its source at the exact release tag). generate-notices.mjs names a malformed entry as a problem.

platform (PG-D3, PG-D10, PG-D36 (3); T1 R4, R5): named components with their licence text pinned by SHA-256. kind separate-program: a program we only run or that wraps our files (aggregation, not combination; Inno Setup and Pascal Script). kind toolchain-runtime: runtime objects the toolchain links into every binary (the mingw-w64 runtime clarification of PG-D10; LLVM's libunwind and LLVM's compiler-rt, one entry each because each has its own LICENSE.TXT). kind upstream-binary: an upstream's own unmodified release binary, recorded with the fields of upstream-binary.schema.json: name, version, licence, source, read, licence_file, sha256 (of the text), file, file_sha256, upstream, links_microsoft_runtime (static|import|none; microsoft_runtime_dlls and installer_runtime_check true as well where it is import), passes_on (the conditions it passes on, kept as it states them), passes_on_kind (none|listed-restrictions), passes_on_source, duties and why; source_ref is optional. One that passes on an indemnity or a duty to make users accept further terms does not ship: the schema refuses those words in passes_on, and `check-licences.mjs --format platform` applies the same word screen (PASSES_ON_REFUSED) and also refuses every passes_on_kind but none and listed-restrictions, a missing one included, and kind none with a non-empty passes_on, and listed-restrictions with an empty passes_on or no passes_on_source. Any platform entry may carry about_line, a non-empty string: the line its licence asks for, which generate-notices.mjs writes under "Required acknowledgements" in every notices file; the template's RemObjects Pascal Script entry carries the installer contract's wording, which the installer checker's IC-18 accepts (an app with no installer deletes that entry). licence_file is the path of the pinned text from the repository root (or ~/); the template's own entries point into .github/licence-texts/, where each text is kept byte for byte as its source publishes it (never reformatted or given other line endings: the folder's own .gitattributes, `* -text`, keeps git from changing a line ending), and source is the URL of that file at an exact commit (the commit of the release tag where the upstream tags its releases; the mingw-w64 commit has no tag), with read (YYYY-MM-DD) and source_ref saying how the commit was found. No text there ends in .md, so no Markdown linter or spell check reads a text that is not ours. A text of an upstream binary goes in the same folder. The record format of an upstream binary is upstream-binary.schema.json in the workspace's knowledge/templates/records/; an upstream binary also pins its own file by file_sha256, with file a path relative to the folder the build vendors upstream binaries into. sha256 or file_sha256 null means not pinned yet. `node .github/scripts/check-licences.mjs --format platform` fails on every unpinned entry and on every licence text that no longer hashes to its pin; it is the `Toolchain and upstream-binary records` step of the licence job in ci-rust.yml (supply-chain) and the `Platform records` step of ci-dotnet.yml (licences). With --upstream-dir, the package job checks every vendored binary against its record (PG-D36 (3)).

denied_components (PG-D31; licensing.md §2.6): packages whose presence fails the gate whatever their licence, because they implement a format whose patent holders license it for money, or one that a pool also licenses. The package names are a starting set (inference: crate and npm names as known when this was written). The string scan of the shipped binaries is the backstop: `check-licences.mjs --format scan`, the `Denied-codec string scan` step of ci-rust.yml's package job, fails a binary that holds a scan_strings entry. scan_exempt names the one place a string is allowed, which is never a download of ours (PG-D37), so the scan applies no exemption.
denied_features (PG-D6, PG-D31): crate features that must stay off. Generated into deny.toml [[bans.features]].

own_sources (S-27; licensing.md §0, §3.3, §3.16): { ecosystem: cargo, source (the https git URL of the repository), crates: [names], licence, why }. Luka's own crates fetched from another of his repositories: the S-27 kit crates (`kit-*`) from their shared home and the S-01 crate once it leaves PerfWindow. They are admitted by source, not by licence: each source joins rust.allow_git, and each crate gets its own exception for its licence in deny.toml, about.toml and the dependency review, while class L stays as the profile has it. In a gpl-le program they are covered by that program's own §7 permission (PW-D12, IN-D13), which is why profile_reasons' rule against third-party GPL code does not apply to them (inference, the S-27 licensing rule of 2026-11-18). Only the gpl and gpl-le profiles take them, and the licence must be GPL-3.0-or-later (optionally WITH an exception). Never list a third party's crate here.
rust: settings that only deny.toml and about.toml use: build targets (PG-D10), RustSec advisories ignored with { id, reason } (each names the condition that retires it), and allowed git sources.
generate: the files licence-configs.mjs writes and checks; delete the entries this repository's stacks do not use.

classes.L: linked, compiled or bundled code: every package-manager dependency, and vendored code under third_party/
classes.F: fonts shipped in a program, a package or a site
classes.C: content and data: images, icons, audio, video, 3D, texts, datasets
classes.M: model weights with their tokenizer and configuration files: pointer-only (PG-D33)
classes.P: platform components: separate programs, toolchain runtimes and upstream binaries, each a named platform entry
classes.T: build and CI tools, never shipped: only the licence for our own use matters (T1 §2.6)

deny.CC-BY-NC-*: non-commercial: the FSF calls it non-free and Fedora does not allow it; our GPL lets every recipient sell copies, so an NC file in the same download breaks that promise. Tier 2 at most, as a pointer the user fetches (PG-D2; T1 §2.4)
deny.CC-BY-ND-*: no derivatives, while our licences grant modification (T1 §2.4)
deny.SSPL-1.0: offering the program as a service requires releasing the whole service's source (§13); not OSI-approved (T1 §2.4)
deny.BUSL-1.1: only non-production use until the Change Date (T1 §2.4)
deny.*OpenRAIL*: behavioural-use licence: its restrictions must flow down as enforceable terms and the licensor may restrict use remotely. Tier 2 at most (PG-D2; T1 §2.4)
deny.Llama*: custom model licence with a user threshold that requires asking Meta for a licence. Tier 2 at most (PG-D2; T1 §2.4)
deny.Gemma*: Gemma Terms of Use: flow-down use restrictions and a remote-restriction right. Tier 2 at most (PG-D2; T1 §2.4)
deny.LFM*: revenue threshold above which a commercial licence is required. Tier 2 at most (PG-D2; T1 §2.4)
deny.JSON: "shall be used for Good, not Evil" is a use restriction (FSF; T1 §2.4)
deny.Ubuntu-font-1.0: Debian ships it only in non-free and Fedora does not allow it; egui apps build eframe without default_fonts and load their own OFL fonts (PG-D6; T1 R11)
deny.LicenseRef-ubuntu-font-1.0: Fedora's id for the Ubuntu Font Licence (PG-D6; T1 R11)
deny.NOASSERTION: no licence stated: without a licence the default copyright law applies, so there is no permission (T1 §2.4)
deny.UNKNOWN: no licence found: no permission until a clarification records the true licence with evidence (PG-D2)
deny.UNLICENSED: npm's mark for a package that grants no licence (T1 §2.4)
deny.GPL-2.0-only: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #GPLv2); fine for a separate program we only run (platform entry, T1 R4)
deny.GPL-2.0: the deprecated id of GPL-2.0-only: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #GPLv2)
deny.AGPL-3.0-only: changes the duties of the whole program (source for network users); no project uses an AGPL profile (PG-D1)
deny.AGPL-3.0-or-later: changes the duties of the whole program (source for network users); no project uses an AGPL profile (PG-D1)
deny.CDDL-1.0: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #CDDL); fine for a separate program
deny.CDDL-1.1: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #CDDL); fine for a separate program
deny.EPL-1.0: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #EPL); fine for a separate program
deny.EPL-2.0: GPL-incompatible in linked code unless GPL is named as a secondary licence, which an OR expression shows (FSF #EPL2)
deny.MPL-2.0-no-copyleft-exception: MPL-2.0 with Exhibit B refuses the secondary-licence route into the GPL (T1 §2.3.1)
deny.OpenSSL: the old OpenSSL licence is GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #OpenSSL)
deny.LPPL-1.3a: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #LPPL-1.3a); TeX packages are class T for the CV
deny.LPPL-1.3c: GPL-incompatible in linked code (FSF #LPPL-1.3a); TeX packages are class T for the CV
deny.EUPL-1.1: copyleft incompatible with the GPL except through a relicensing judgement, which the gate does not make (FSF #EUPL-1.2)
deny.EUPL-1.2: copyleft incompatible with the GPL except through a relicensing judgement, which the gate does not make (FSF #EUPL-1.2)

gpl-le.GPL-*: a gpl-le program takes no third-party GPL code: only the copyright holder can grant the linking exception (GPL FAQ #GPLIncompatibleLibs), and asking is contact (AP §1; T1 §2.3.1)
gpl-le.LGPL-*: a gpl-le program takes LGPL only as a separately loaded library named in lgpl_dynamic (T1 R2)

reserved.*GPL*: the CV is all rights reserved: no LGPL or GPL code is bundled into it (T1 R2)

permissive.GPL-*: a repository not yet relicensed takes no GPL code until its relicensing merges (T1 R2)

LicenseRef-Microsoft-WindowsAppSDK.meaning: Microsoft's licence terms for the Windows App SDK packages, a licence file (license.txt) in each package that has no SPDX id. 2.0.x ships these packages inside its self-contained build, the transition of PG-D20 (RF-D22, RF-D26, RF-D28). It is allowed on the permissive profile's class L list for this release line only; 3.0.0 ships none of them and the id leaves the policy with them

LicenseRef-Microsoft-WindowsSDK-BuildToo.meaning: Microsoft's Windows SDK licence terms for the SDK build-tool packages that the WinUI build restores as build-time tools that are never shipped. The policy machinery cannot put a NuGet package in class T (class_overrides takes F or C only), so they are judged in class L and the id sits on the permissive profile's list beside the Windows App SDK's

LicenseRef-Public-Domain.meaning: a term expired under both Serbian and EU rules, or the holding institution's own CC0 or PDM release (PG-D32 (B); T1 §2.3.3)

LicenseRef-PD-USGov.meaning: a US federal work (17 U.S.C. §105): a US-only basis that never stands alone (PG-D32)

LicenseRef-Public-Domain-US-Government.meaning: a US federal work (17 U.S.C. §105): a US-only basis that never stands alone (PG-D32)

LicenseRef-RemObjects-PascalScript.meaning: RemObjects Pascal Script's licence, compiled into Inno Setup's setup stub; its text is pinned in the platform entry (PG-D3; IN-D26)

LicenseRef-mingw-w64-runtime.meaning: the compound COPYING.MinGW-w64-runtime.txt, carried whole; pinned in the platform entry (PG-D10)

the package's own license.txt, Microsoft's Windows App SDK terms (the same text in all four packages); shipped by 2.0.x under PG-D20's transition (RF-D22, RF-D28)

build-time tool, never shipped; the package's own sdk_license.txt, Microsoft's Windows SDK terms

licence_texts.source: https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64/10.0.15 (LICENSE.TXT, the MIT text of the .NET runtime); the System.* packages below declare MIT in their nuspec and ship no licence file of their own

platform.name: Inno Setup
platform.source_ref: jrsoftware/issrc tag is-7_1_1 = commit 2527da77ff7983514f535d19391a748c5d898336; the file equals license.txt of the 7.1.1 install (same SHA-256)
duties: keep every copyright notice and web address in place (About box, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)
mark modified versions plainly: Inno Setup is used unmodified
platform.why: the installer's setup stub and uninstaller ship inside every installer; Inno wraps our files and is not linked with them (T1 R4; PS-D9, IN-D26). spdx.org lists the id InnoSetup (PH-D76). Its purchase page asks only commercial users to buy a licence; no project is commercial (AP §1), so nothing is owed or bought (PS-D9). In CI it comes from the vendor's download, pinned by URL and SHA-256 (RF-D38).

platform.source_ref: jrsoftware/issrc tag is-7_1_1 = commit 2527da77ff7983514f535d19391a748c5d898336, Components/UniPs/LICENSE.md: the copy that Inno Setup 7.1.1 compiles in; committed byte for byte under a .txt name, so that no Markdown linter or spell check reads a text that is not ours (its second line holds tabs)

denied_components.reason: H.264 and HEVC are licensed for money by their patent holders: no program ships an implementation of them, and none ever ships an encoder; they are reached only through what Windows or the user already has (PG-D31)
denied_components.scan_exempt: OpenH264 inside the Electron that Nexus's installer fetches from Electron's publisher; Nexus switches it off at start and ships none of it (PG-D37)

denied_components.reason: the AAC family is licensed for money by its patent holders (PG-D31)
a full FFmpeg build carries H.264, HEVC and AAC code (PG-D31)
denied_components.scan_exempt: the codec-free FFmpeg zip that Nexus's installer fetches from Electron's release page (PG-D37)

denied_components.component: AV1, VP8, VP9 and Opus codecs
denied_components.reason: their developers grant them royalty-free, but third parties also license them through a pool or a signed programme, so they are not bundled and are reached through Windows (PG-D31)
denied_components.scan_exempt: inside Chromium in the Electron that Nexus's installer fetches, which holds Opus, VP8, VP9 and AV1 code that Chromium cannot switch off (PG-D31 residual, PG-D37)

denied_components.reason: lossy WebP is VP8, which a pool also licenses (PG-D31; T8 F14, F15); lossless WebP goes through Windows (WIC) or a lossless-only decoder
denied_components.scan_exempt: a libwebp built with no VP8 code, for lossless WebP output only, if Contextool's S-I1 finds no WIC WebP encoder (CT-D18, PG-D31; whether libwebp builds that way was not checked). Contextool removes this entry only once its build is shown to hold no VP8 code, and records that in docs/format-sources.md

denied_features.reason: brings the Ubuntu font (Ubuntu-font-1.0); every egui app sets default-features = false and loads its own OFL fonts (PG-D6)
another crate can turn the fonts back on through feature unification (PG-D6; T1 R11)
the crate that holds the default fonts behind the feature (inference; PG-D6)

pulls image-webp, which holds a lossy VP8 decoder (R1 §2.10; PG-D31): an app that uses image enables PNG and JPEG only. PeepHole, whose register decodes lossless WebP (VP8L) through image and checks the VP8 or VP8L chunk before decoding (PH-D18; spec Formats, v1), removes this entry at adoption; no other repository does
